bindings.label: An 80-year-old woman presented with difficulty raising her right upper limb, progressive dyskinesia, gait disorder, neck pain, and numbness in her extremities
She had neck pain for approximately 2 years and numbness in her extremities for about 1 year, both significantly worsened before her visit; she could walk unassisted for less than 100 meters

Physical examination showed muscle weakness (MMT score 3) in the entire right upper limb, normal strength in the remaining limbs, hypesthesia throughout the upper and lower limbs, increased deep tendon reflexes bilaterally in all limbs, positive Hoffman's and Wartenberg's signs, and preoperative JOA score 8.5 points

Radiographs and cervical contrast CT revealed osteolytic lesions in C3-7; a mass extended into the spinal canal from within the vertebrae, compressing the cervical spinal cord from the right side; the mass was stained in the early contrast phase and showed an internal low-density area; MRI detected a mass with the same signal profile as bone from within the C3-7 vertebrae to outside of the vertebral bodies, compressing the cervical spinal cord from the right side at the same levels

Blood tests showed no thrombocytopenia, anemia, or coagulation abnormalities; inflammatory response was normal; blood cultures and various tumor markers were negative; percutaneous vertebral biopsy showed culture negativity and no neoplastic lesions
Cervical spine neoplasm
Spinal infection/inflammation
Non-neoplastic bone lesion
Biopsy shows atypical vasoforming proliferation with ERG, CD31, and CD34 positivity
Biopsy shows pericytic markers myo1B, CD146, and SMA positivity and is negative for D2-40, CAMTA1, TFE3, and FOSB
Ki-67 proliferation index in biopsy is approximately 16.1% and 10.6%
Biopsy specimen shows infiltration into surrounding muscle and fat
Cervical spine vascular neoplasm
Pathologist recommends tumor subtyping with oncology and spine surgery correlation
Radiologist recommends contrast-enhanced MRI/MRA to assess vascular supply and multidisciplinary management
Cervical spine vascular neoplasm with locally aggressive behavior
Cervical spine angiosarcoma (malignant vascular neoplasm)
Cervical spine epithelioid hemangioendothelioma
Aggressive cervical vertebral hemangioma
Cervical spine hemangioblastoma
Cervical spine Kaposi sarcoma
Pathologist reports angiosarcoma is the leading diagnosis
Pathologist states negative EHE markers exclude epithelioid hemangioendothelioma
